title: AI-Driven Biometric Animal Registration for Animal Welfare and Global Health
summary: iSciLab describes horse-passport and vaccination-tracking pilots, aiming to improve animal identification, welfare, and disease surveillance.
source_collection: ITU AI for Good: Innovate for Impact (2025)
account: The biometric registration project uses nose prints and facial features to identify animals without invasive tags. The submission lists a Korean horse-passport pilot and African field testing for rabies tracking. It describes intended management and welfare benefits, without quantified identification, vaccination, or disease outcomes.
purpose: Improve non-invasive animal identification and traceability.
location: South Korea and unspecified African field-test settings

ratings.reason: Korean horse-passport and African vaccination-tracking pilots are listed without measured management improvements.
Animal welfare, rabies prevention, and reduced illegal trade are proposed effects rather than observed outcomes.

ai_role.statement: The contributor describes the system and its proposed or reported contribution. This collection entry does not independently isolate the effect of AI from the surrounding workflow.

evidence.citation: Contributed use case in International Telecommunication Union, AI for Good: Innovate for Impact, 2025. Information current as of June 2025. The reported outcomes are attributed to the submitting project, not an independent outcome evaluation by ITU.
evidence.title: Use Case 5: AI-Driven Biometric Animal Registration for Animal Welfare and Global Health

produced_by: The contributor describes the application and its setting in the cited entry. Conditions sufficient to reproduce the reported benefit have not been established.
must_hold: Requirements for reproducing the benefit need to be evaluated in the new setting. The collection entry does not establish that its reported results will recur.

headline: Animal biometrics support registration and vaccination tracking

revisions.change: Added the sourced case with separate benefit depth, beneficiary, evidence confidence, and outcome status assessments.

claim_basis: The makers' report is on file. There is no independent source and no finding by a regulator or court.
